reviews.summary:
I walked the tree as the 62-year-old German patient with chronic back pain. My treatment is easy to find, the doctors and villa prices are not, and the plan's moves put the breadcrumb out of step with the left rail on 13 pages.

To check the real ordering, I ran a copy of tools/build-site-tree.mjs in scratchpad with the plan's overrides applied. It completed: 216 pages in 15 sections, every indexable route once, 0 dead links. I did not touch the repo.

What worked and what did not, need by need:

- **My treatment:** easy. Treatments & programmes › Ayurvedic treatments › Joints, back & spine › 'Chronic & lower back pain'. The condition-first labels match each programme's own 'For:' line on the finder.
- **The villas:** easy to find, but no prices anywhere in that section. The only page with per-night rates by villa (/ayurvedic-treatment-packages.html) is filed under Treatments.
- **Prices and offers:** spread across three sections. The Offers hub shows 13 visible '[TO CONFIRM]' placeholders. The FAQ page's new label promotes price lists titled 2025–26 and last updated April 2025.
- **How to get there:** easy (Plan your visit › How to reach us). But that section is 11th of 15 on /sitemap/, and /map/ gives travel times that contradict How to reach.
- **The doctors:** not findable by label. The only physician panel (Dr. Deepu John and two BAMS physicians) is on /online-consultation/, labelled as a consultation booking.
- **FAQs:** easy (58 questions under Plan your visit).

Problems the plan creates:

- **Breadcrumbs:** 13 of the 63 moves put a page in a new section while its visible breadcrumb still names the old one. For example, /meditation/ reads 'Home / Knowledge Centre' at the top while its rail says Things to do.
- **Misgrouped programme:** the programme 'for more than one condition' sits inside the detox group.
- **Weight article:** an older article with unsigned claims ('no need for exercise or diet limits') becomes a sub-page of the clinical weight programme.
- **Uneven rule for activities:** cooking classes and animal husbandry are left out of 'Things to do in the village', although the plan used the same evidence to move yoga classes, walks and meditation there.
- **Yoga labels:** '7-night minimum' does not tell the training page apart from the yoga package, which is also 7 nights and has the same starting price.

In parts of the tree the plan did not touch:

- The /gallery/ hub cards link to "0" to "7", so they are dead links.
- /photo-gallery/ links five sub-galleries, so it could be their parent (it is currently left flat).
- Payment and cancellation terms sit in the policies bucket instead of Plan your visit.
- Villas, the training course ladder and the sightseeing distance bands appear in a confusing order.
- /training-course-fees/ and /attractions-above-50kms/ show leaked build text to visitors.

For the owner, not fixed (HARD GATE 6): the Deluxe single rate per night differs across three pages (₹16,264, ₹17,786 and ₹18,410).

Working files are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Volumes-Extreme-SSD---Blue-2nd-Kairali-Digital--codex-worktrees-ahv-english-staging-20260915/7c3bed3a-cb76-4f54-8126-8678f51add5a/scratchpad/ia/review/:

reviews.summary:
I read the prerendered page for every moved or relabelled page, the hubs they depend on, and the current tree, and applied the plan in a simulation. The plan is mostly sound: every parent exists, no label contains a locked word, drops create no dead links, and most placements match the pages. Several of the architect's claims checked out: the five course pages link back to /ayurveda-training-programme/ as 'all courses', /experience/ links all seven rule pages, /product-range/ links its seven ranges, the in-village and Kerala hubs link their activities, and each gallery's photo captions match its new label.

Objections, most serious first:

1. **Two clinical labels name conditions the programme pages never mention.** The page for 'Slipped disc & sciatica' has no mention of sciatica, and the page for 'Nerve disorders & neuropathy' has no mention of neuropathy or numbness. Both terms come only from the finder 'For:' lines, and the vocabulary behind those lines is still marked PENDING clinical sign-off. Separately, the 'cholesterol' in 'High blood pressure & cholesterol' is a single benefit bullet on a page about hypertension and heart health.

2. **Placements made from a title, not the page:**
   - /organic-farm/ is filed under 'Village house rules' because /experience/ has an 'Organic Farming' card, but the page is about a farm visitors can tour.
   - The weight-management article is nested under the weight-loss programme. That programme page is not a hub and does not link it. The article also claims weight loss 'without dietary limitations', which contradicts the programme's structured diet.

3. **Labels resting on false distinctions:**
   - 'Packages to book online': every programme page has the same Book Now link to the booking site.
   - 'Apply for a job or internship': the form is job-only, and the claim that the internships page links to it is wrong. Its Apply Now link actually goes to /new-to-ayurveda/.
   - The 'training' in the 7-night yoga label: the plan itself says the two twin pages differ only in minimum stay.

4. **The builder sorts children by route-manifest order,** so the duration ladder (20, 5, 10, 1, 3 days), the distance bands and 'Why visit Kerala' will render out of order unless the plan ships an explicit order.

5. **Two drops break the owner's drop rule:** /prav-simona-yoga-retreat/ and /special-offers/ have real content.

6. **Smaller items (low severity):**
   - A few labels overclaim or are unclear: the doshas label on /learn-about-ayurveda/, 'for all ages' on a page written for midlife readers, 'within 10 km' on a page listing a place 14 km away, 'Japan group' on the workshop itinerary.
   - The sign-off note to Dr. Deepu John says 31 programmes; the tree has 29.
   - The 2025-26 price lists behind the new 'price lists' labels have a tariff the site says runs out on 30 September 2026.
   - Six more parents that don't link their new children, and two wrong links on the /village-facilities/ hub.
   - /new-privacy-policy/ is served and indexable but missing from the tree: a third privacy document.

Working files are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Volumes-Extreme-SSD---Blue-2nd-Kairali-Digital--codex-worktrees-ahv-english-staging-20260915/7c3bed3a-cb76-4f54-8126-8678f51add5a/scratchpad/audit/: txt/*.txt holds the extracted page text, dump.py produced it, and after-tree.txt is the simulated tree after the plan.

reviews.summary:
I checked the plan against the pages' actual content and links, not just their titles. I rendered the tree the plan would produce (scratchpad/ia/plan/final.json), re-ran the builder's sort order against route-manifest.json, and listed the in-page links of every hub from the prerenders. I also read tools/build-site-tree.mjs, tools/build-section-nav.mjs and public/design/section-nav.js, and read the pages behind each disputed placement.

The plan's basic hard rules hold. Every parent exists and sits in the same section, nothing loops, no label contains a locked word, and no listed path redirects (checked against redirect-map.json and the deferred list). Most of its reshaping holds up against the content: the programme labels come from each programme's own 'For:' line, the house-rules hub /experience/ really does link its rule pages, the products ladder follows /product-range/'s own links, the yoga classes and meditation belong with in-village activities, and the Japan workshop is correctly filed as a past group visit.

Problems the plan creates or leaves in place:

1. **Dropped pages lose their navigation (high).** Once a page is dropped, the rail no longer runs there, so the old WordPress sidebar is not removed. On 9 pages that currently show the rail, this brings back a 'Knowledge Center' menu on offers and programmes pages, or old context menus.
2. **Children are shown out of order.** The builder sorts by manifest position, so the course ladder reads 20, 5, 10, 1, 3 days and the distance bands read 15, 25–50, 50+, 10 km. The bands show that way on every band page's rail.
3. **The weight article is filed under a programme page, which is not a hub.** Nothing links it from there, and the grouped finder makes its rail show 8 dead concern headings.
4. **/photo-gallery/ is a real hub that the plan ignores.** It links five galleries that the /gallery/ hub can't reach (its card links are broken), yet Gallery stays an 11-item flat list.
5. **/destination-palakkad/ is left as a one-page orphan**, although /things-to-do-in-kerala/ links it. The plan used that same kind of link to move /visit-kerala/.
6. **/organic-farm/ is misfiled as a house rule**, and /animal-husbandry/ is stranded alone at the Facilities root.
7. **The yoga labels do not tell the pages apart.** The '7-night' programme and the package have the same minimum stay and the same from-price. 'Training' clashes with the Training section, and the register calls /yoga-meditation-training/ 'yoga teacher training', which is an open fact for the owner.
8. **Smaller items (low severity).** Two near-duplicate treatment lists sit at the programmes first level. The plan's suggested builder fix for Karkidaka would not work, because Karkidaka is not in the programme register. Several other branches (Kerala, villas, New to Ayurveda, training, past retreats) are also sorted by path. The product range pages sit four levels deep in a 300px rail.

Every fix uses paths that exist in the current tree.

proposals.about: Seasonal monsoon programme, Karkidaka Chikitsa (Karkidakam month, July to August): Panchakarma, Rasayana and Karkidaka Kanji in 7, 14 or 21-day options, with an enquiry form.

Copy defect: one card title reads 'Spine Care & Spondylitis Treatmentralysis'.

proposals.about: Short opinion essay (365 words) on why busy, stressed working people benefit from a yoga retreat, praising Kairali's village. It has no programme details: no durations, inclusions or prices.
